exposure: smoking status (never vs. former vs. current)
outcome: urgency (any urgency in the past 7 days)
moderate urgency (urgency at least half the time)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 1720 community-based adult women recruited via the ResearchMatch website who completed an online survey of bladder health.
finding: Current smoking status was strongly associated with a higher risk of experiencing urgency, moderate urgency, and urgency urinary incontinence (UUI), while a lifetime history of 20+ pack years was also significantly associated with all urgency outcomes in smokers/former smokers.
cross-section timing: Symptoms of urgency were assessed for the past 7 days at the time of the online survey.
